sections.h2: What should an owner know before selling a house in Kiryas Joel, NY?
sections.html:
Kiryas Joel is a very small, very dense village in Orange County, and its housing market is tight enough that the 2020 census counted a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.1% and a rental vacancy rate of 2.5%. That 2020 count found 6,207 housing units with 6.0% vacant and 5,837 households.

In the 2020-2024 survey the typical owned home is worth $758,800, and 33.4% of households own. Median gross rent is $1,604. Households average 5.08 people, so bedroom counts and room layout carry weight. Owners selling should be ready to describe bedrooms, kitchens and any additions.

  • Check that every addition and finished space has a closed permit and a certificate of occupancy.
  • Collect water and sanitation, village tax and town and county tax paperwork before the contract.
  • Decide whether you want to market privately, list publicly, or take a cash offer.

sections.h2: Where is Kiryas Joel and which town governs it?
sections.html:
Kiryas Joel is a village in Orange County that is now coterminous with the Town of Palm Tree. The land was bought in the early 1970s by followers of the Satmar rebbe, 14 families settled there in the summer of 1974, and the village incorporated in 1976 out of the Town of Monroe. In 2019 the village separated from Monroe to become the new Town of Palm Tree, which Wikipedia describes as New York's first new town in 38 years.

The village covers 1.1 square miles by total area, and the Census Bureau lists 1.46 square miles of land for 2020 and a density of 22,540.4 people per square mile. A small pond called Forest Road Lake sits in the center. Because the village and the town share one boundary, ask the village which office holds the building and occupancy records for your house, and expect separate village and town bills at tax time.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about households in Kiryas Joel?
sections.html:
The population is young: 55.2% of residents are under 18, and only 2.4% are 65 or older. The 2020 census listed a median age of 14.4 years.

Other 2020-2024 measures help explain what buyers want. A total of 95.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so few households move in a given year. About 92.8% of people age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home, and the 2010 census recorded that 91.5% spoke Yiddish at home. If you are selling, plan for contracts, disclosures and communications to be understood by every party, and ask your attorney whether translation help is worthwhile.

Economic figures show a village with large households and modest per-person income. Median household income is $50,032, per-capita income is $14,440 and the poverty rate is 37.6%. Owners pay a median $2,616 a month with a mortgage and $1,075 without. A seller can expect buyers to ask about carrying costs such as tax and utility bills.

sections.h2: How are taxes and utilities billed in Kiryas Joel?
sections.html:
The village's official site runs a bill-payment page with three separate links: one for water and sanitation, one for the village property tax bill, and one for the town and county property tax bill. That structure tells a seller that closing involves at least three accounts to settle, not one.

Before you sign a contract, ask the village for the current status of each. Your attorney or title company will request tax searches and a water and sanitation reading so that the buyer and seller split the bills fairly on the closing date. Orange County's Department of Finance handles county questions about tax bills and needs the town and tax map identification number for the parcel. A property's assessment is handled by the local assessor, and the county advises contacting your own assessor for assessment questions. Orange County's online parcel search can supply the tax map number if you do not have it.

Because the village and the town are the same area, a tax question may involve both governments. Ask for the paperwork in writing, and keep the receipts with your closing file.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Orange County, and what tax applies?
sections.html:
Deeds for Kiryas Joel properties are filed in the Orange County Clerk's office. The county's FAQ page says questions about filing costs and policies go to the clerk's office, and its phone number there is 845-291-2690.

New York's real estate transfer tax applies on top of recording charges. Article 31 of the Tax Law taxes a conveyance when the consideration exceeds $500, at two dollars for every $500 or fraction, and payment is due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The seller carries the bill, and the buyer owes it only if the seller is exempt or does not pay. On a sale at the $758,800 Census median, the tax would be $3,036. An additional 1% tax applies to residential conveyances of $1 million or more, and it falls on the buyer.

The clerk's office also offers a free Fraud Alert service that notifies property owners when a deed or mortgage is recorded under their name, and it says a copy of your deed costs approximately $5 directly from the office. Online record searching through the clerk's contractor costs $15 for one day of access, with printing at $5 per document. The clerk's page also warns about companies that offer to obtain your deed for a fee.

sections.h2: How do schools factor into a Kiryas Joel sale?
sections.html:
Most children in the village attend private religious schools, with about 12,000 students in them in 2021 and nearly two dozen schools in 2020. The public Kiryas Joel School District runs a school for special-education students and had 165 public students in 2022-23.

With so few children in the public district, the district name carries less weight in a listing than it would in many New York suburbs. The village runs its own bus system, which has service to Manhattan and to Williamsburg and Borough Park in Brooklyn, according to Wikipedia, and the Census Bureau lists the average commute as 18.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a good choice for a Kiryas Joel house?
sections.html:
A cash offer is worth pricing out when you need a fast close, the house needs repair, or an estate must be settled among several heirs. A financed sale to a family buyer may bring a higher price when the house is in good shape and the timeline is flexible.

Whichever route you take, put the terms on paper, settle who covers transfer tax and recording, and have a New York attorney read the contract. Confirm that your certificate of occupancy covers the current number of rooms and units, because an unpermitted conversion can stall closing. Also check the water and sanitation account and both property tax bills so they are current on the closing date.

faqs.q: Which town is Kiryas Joel in?
faqs.a: Kiryas Joel is in the Town of Palm Tree, Orange County. The village was part of the Town of Monroe from 1976 until 2019, when it separated to become the new Town of Palm Tree. The village and the town share the same boundary.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Kiryas Joel house?
faqs.a: Deeds are filed in the Orange County Clerk's office. The county directs questions about filing costs and policies to the clerk at 845-291-2690. The seller's attorney or title company normally prepares and files the deed at closing.

faqs.q: How much is New York transfer tax on a Kiryas Joel sale?
faqs.a: The state tax is $2 for every $500 of the sale price, or fraction of it. On $758,800, which is the Census median value, that comes to $3,036. The seller pays it, and an extra 1% buyer tax applies at $1,000,000 or more for residential property.

faqs.q: What is the population of Kiryas Joel?
faqs.a: The mid-2025 Census estimate is 47,147 residents, up from 32,954 in the 2020 census. The village covers 1.46 square miles of land, so it is among the densest places in the state at 22,540 people per square mile in 2020.

faqs.q: How are the village's bills split when a house sells?
faqs.a: The village lists separate payment links for water and sanitation, village property tax and town and county property tax. Ask each for a current balance before closing, and have your attorney or title company prorate them with the buyer on the closing date.
